evidence: Wanderlog reviews from June 2026 say Vesper (Vinkenstraat 57) was taken over and is becoming SANTO, an all-day concept ('the old Vesper is no more'). Difford's Guide marks the bar permanently closed (undated).
notes: Successor: SANTO at Vinkenstraat 57, Amsterdam. Evidence is user reviews on an aggregator plus Difford's, no news article found; Amsterdamnow page (modified 2026-03-08) still describes the bar in present tense.

name: Pekin Cafe and Lounge Inc.
evidence: Daily Montanan (24 Apr 2026) reports Pekin Noodle Parlor in Butte closed its doors after 117 years, with a closed sign on the door on 24 Apr 2026. Owner said 'There is still a future for the Pekin' but no reopening or new owner is announced.
notes: Name in our data is a company name; real venue is Pekin Noodle Parlor (James Beard America's Classic), Main Street, Butte. Possible future revival not confirmed.

name: Cut by Wolfgang Puck
evidence: Hotel & Catering (29 Dec 2022) reports CUT by Wolfgang Puck at Mondrian Doha closed after five years, partnership ending 1 Jan 2023, with a farewell night on 31 Dec 2022. OpenTable's Mondrian Doha page also says permanently closed (undated).
notes: Mondrian Doha, West Bay Lagoon. A Qatar Tribune piece of 3 Nov 2020 only covers an earlier reopening.

name: Indochine
evidence: What's On Dubai (23 Oct 2023) reports Indochine in DIFC (Gate District Precinct Building 3) has officially closed its doors. No reopening or new Dubai location is named.

name: Lakeside
evidence: Casino.org Vital Vegas (9 Jul 2024, updated 11 Jul 2024) says Lakeside at Wynn Las Vegas would permanently close in mid-July 2024, with Fiola Mare planned for early 2025. Wynn's own 2026 dining page does not list Lakeside.
notes: Successor at Wynn is Fiola Mare (a different business); not confirmed opened.

name: St. Hubertus
evidence: Scatti di Gusto (20 Feb 2023) and Dissapore report St. Hubertus closed on 24 Mar 2023 and would not reopen as before, as Rosa Alpina was renovated with Aman. Aman Rosa Alpina's 2026 site lists The Grill, Enju, Il Salotto and other venues, not St. Hubertus, and says the resort reopens 4 Dec 2026.
notes: Chef Norbert Niederkofler left the kitchen; the hotel is now Aman Rosa Alpina with different restaurants.

name: Belon International Cuisine
evidence: Tatler Asia lists Belon at Banyan Tree Macau (Galaxy Macau, Cotai) as 'Permanently closed' (page footer 2026). Banyan Tree Macau's own dining page lists only Saffron, Cabana and Banyan Lounge, with no Belon.
notes: No dated closure announcement found. Macau.com still lists hours but is undated.

name: COI
evidence: Wikipedia lists Coi as closed in 2022, citing an SFGate article dated 15 Mar 2022 ('Michelin-starred SF restaurant closes'). No reopening mentioned.
notes: SFGate article itself not opened.

name: Re -
evidence: Concrete Playground's page for Re (South Eveleigh) is titled 'Re - CLOSED' and was last updated 13 Mar 2024. No closing date or successor given.
notes: Name is 'Re' (Matt Whiley, Maurice Terzini). Single source.

name: Alain Ducasse au Plaza Athénée
evidence: Gambero Rosso International (May 2021) reports Ducasse's restaurant at the Plaza Athénée would close on 30 June 2021 when his 21-year lease ended; Jean Imbert was expected to take over. Dissapore also ran the departure story.
notes: Successor (Jean Imbert au Plaza Athénée) was only 'expected' in the source. Ducasse remains at Le Meurice.

name: Dialogue
evidence: Wikipedia says Dialogue (1315 3rd Street Promenade) closed on 7 Nov 2020, citing an Eater LA article of 25 Oct 2020 announcing the closing. No relocation or reopening mentioned.
notes: Eater LA article itself not opened.

name: The NoMad Bar
evidence: Hot Dinners (2021-11-17) reports the NoMad hotel at 1170 Broadway is closing permanently and being taken over by The Ned; Travel Weekly says the hotel's restaurant and bars had stopped service. A Flatiron/NoMad news roundup (2022-08-02) says The Ned NoMad has opened at 1170 Broadway.
notes: The Daniel Humm/Will Guidara NoMad Bar went with the hotel; no source shows it was revived. The Ned NoMad is a separate business on the site; its current status was not verified (thened.com could not be fetched). The Ritz-Carlton New York, NoMad (25 W 28th St) is an unrelated hotel.

name: The Silver Dollar
evidence: A Nov 28, 2025 article says the bar at 1761 Frankfort Avenue closed for good after 14 years, with a final farewell service on Saturday Nov 15 (2025). No later reopening seen.
notes: Single named news source plus aggregator listings; the Nov 15 date is a Saturday in 2025.

name: Veladora
evidence: Rancho Valencia's own site (last modified 2026-11-01, 2026 Forbes awards) names The Pony Room as its signature restaurant (Coastal Ranch cuisine) and does not mention Veladora; its dining page lists only Pony Room and Rein. Gayot marks Veladora 'THIS RESTAURANT IS CLOSED' (undated); OpenTable page is stale with 2020 reviews.
notes: Located at Rancho Valencia Resort, 5921 Valencia Circle, Rancho Santa Fe CA (San Diego area). Likely replaced or renamed by The Pony Room; no source states the rename directly. Afar (2022) lists 'Veladora Coastal Ranch'.

name: Operation Dagger
evidence: A Dec 14, 2021 Lady Iron Chef article says Operation Dagger would 'reopen in a new form' as DAGGER at 76 Neil Road (due early 2022). Burpple and Difford's list it as closed (undated).
notes: Original at 7 Ann Siang Hill. A singapore-spirit.com SEO guide (dated 2026-10-22) still lists Operation Dagger at 7 Ann Siang Hill, but it looks like a generic listicle and is not trusted. Successor DAGGER at 76 Neil Road: current status not verified.

name: Tickets
evidence: Big Hospitality (2021-04-12) reports Albert Adria closed Tickets along with Hoja Santa, Pakta and Bodega 1900. A June 18, 2022 Identita Golose article says the space reopened March 15 (2022) as Teatro under new ownership.
notes: Successor business Teatro (owner Manuel Lao, Iglesias brothers direct) at the same site; it is a renamed, re-owned business, not Tickets. Time Out lists Tickets as CLOSED.

name: Blacktail
evidence: Tribeca Citizen reported 'BlackTail at Pier A closing on Saturday' (Jan 9, 2020); OpenTable shows 'permanently closed' (22 Battery Pl) and The Infatuation also says permanently closed. Time Out (Apr 2024) covered only a 3-month May-July 2024 pop-up revival at Back Bar.
notes: Original at Pier A Harbor House, 22 Battery Place. The 2024 residency was temporary; no permanent reopening seen. Blacktail's own site could not be fetched.

name: Dandelyan
evidence: Time Out note added March 2019: 'Dandelyan is now closed'. Hot Dinners (2019-03-29) says Mr Lyan announced the closure in Oct 2018 and the bar closed in March 2019, replaced by Lyaness at Sea Containers, 20 Upper Ground.
notes: Successor Lyaness (same team, same room at Sea Containers, a new concept). Current Lyaness status not checked.

name: De Maria
evidence: Time Out lists 'De Maria (CLOSED)'; NYC Tourism labels it 'Out of Business'; MeltingButter (modified 2018-09-13) carries the note 'De Maria NYC has been reported closed'. No source gives a closure date.
notes: Was at 19 Kenmare St, Nolita. Several independent listings agree but none is dated 2025 or 2026, and the venue's own site (demarianyc.com) now shows unrelated content. Strength is medium on agreement alone.

name: Lost Lake
evidence: Time Out Chicago (Jan 7, 2022) reports Lost Lake at 3154 W Diversey closed permanently after final service Jan 15, 2022; Difford's also lists it permanently closed.
notes: Owners said they might return 'in one form or another'; no return found. Paul McGee's Secret Sound (Time Out Market) is a separate bar.

name: Imperial Cocktail Bar
evidence: Second read: Ynetnews (18 Oct 2025): Imperial to close at the end of the month after 13 years, building to be demolished. The batch verdict OPEN/weak was wrong.

name: Relae
evidence: A post dated 6 Oct 2020 titled 'Relae Christian Puglisi Closes His Restaurant After 10 Years'; a Foodle review says its final dinner was 2 Dec 2020 and the restaurant closed at the end of 2020 (page shows Permanently Closed).
notes: At Jaegersborggade 41. Puglisi's other venues are separate businesses.

name: Restaurant ANDRE
evidence: CNN (Oct 11, 2017) reports last service on Feb 14, 2018 and the site to be redeveloped under a different, more relaxed concept without Chiang's name; Time Out Singapore lists it as CLOSED.
notes: Was at 41 Bukit Pasoh Road. Chiang's later Taiwan venues are separate. No reopening found.

name: The Gibson
evidence: The Spirits Business (2025-12-23) reports new bar The Prince opened (official opening 2 Jan 2026) at 44 Old Street, 'where The Gibson once was'. Difford's lists The Gibson as permanently closed and a forum entry says it is 'sadly now shuttered'.
notes: The Prince is a new business at the Gibson site; not the venue. Closure date not found.

name: Biko
evidence: Time Out Mexico (2017-12-15) says Biko would close Dec 23, 2017 at Masaryk 407, Polanco (plaza demolition) and look for a new site; Forbes Mexico (2018-08-17) says Biko closed and would 'soon reopen elsewhere'. Wikipedia and Time Out list it as closed.
notes: The original closed. A relocation was promised in 2018 but I found no source on whether Biko reopened at a new address; biko.com.mx could not be fetched. Needs a manual check for a post-2018 reopening.

name: Fäviken
evidence: The Local (2019-05-07) reports Magnus Nilsson announced Fäviken would close for good after Dec 14, 2019; Wikipedia says it closed on that date and mentions no reopening.
notes: Search results also showed a 'Fäviken Magasinet' hotel listing; I did not verify whether the estate offers any dining now.

name: Lucques
evidence: Time Out Los Angeles (2020-03-11) reports Suzanne Goin and Caroline Styne announced Lucques would close, final service May 6, 2020; Time Out lists it as CLOSED and Gayot also says closed.
notes: Was at 8474 Melrose Ave, West Hollywood. No reopening found.

name: Oxheart
evidence: PaperCity (2016-12-02) reports Oxheart closing for good March 15, 2017 to be replaced by a new restaurant in the same space; Bisnow (2017-06-05) confirms Oxheart closed and Justin Yu's next restaurant is Theodore Rex. Gayot marks it closed.
notes: Successor Theodore Rex used the Nance Street space; that is a different business. Theodore Rex's own status was not checked.

name: The Bachelor Farmer Cafe
evidence: MPR News (2020-05-01), CBS Minnesota and Minnesota Monthly report The Bachelor Farmer, its cafe and Marvel Bar closing permanently after COVID; Minnesota Monthly's update of March 5, 2021 notes the building is for sale. Axios (2021-01-28) says owner Eric Dayton has no plans to bring it back.
notes: Located in the North Loop, 50 N 2nd Ave. Name in our data is the cafe; the whole complex closed.

name: The Walker Inn
evidence: OpenTable (2026 page) says The Walker Inn at 3612 W 6th St is permanently closed; Time Out and Gayot also mark it CLOSED (undated). The Normandie Club's own site shows it open daily 6pm-2am but does not mention Walker Inn.
notes: Walker Inn was the reservation-only room at Hotel Normandie next to The Normandie Club (the Normandie Club is open and is a separate venue). Closure date not found; no dated news source.

name: The Whale Wins
evidence: Secret Seattle (July 2025) reports Renee Erickson's The Whale Wins closing permanently on Tuesday Oct 28, 2025 because the lease would not be renewed; a 2026-03 Wikipedia mirror says it permanently closed in late October 2025.
notes: The Seattle Met page from July 2025 could not be fetched. Wine club pickups moved to Westward.

name: White Lyan
evidence: Time Out London note (July 2017): 'White Lyan has now closed. New bar Super Lyan has opened in the basement.' The Drinks Business (2016-09) had announced the planned closure.
notes: Successor Super Lyan was in the basement of the same Hoxton building (Kimpton Fitzroy later); a different concept. Super Lyan status not checked.

name: Pouring Ribbons
evidence: EV Grieve (2022-04-04) reports Pouring Ribbons at 225 Avenue B closed for good as of 2022-03-26 when the lease expired; closure was announced Sept 2021. An omakase bar-restaurant (11 Tigers) was planned for the space.
notes: Successor on the site is a different business (11 Tigers).

name: Milk & Honey
evidence: Time Out London (2020-09-28) reports Milk & Honey on Poland Street, Soho, closed for good after its final weekend ending 2020-09-27; landlords repossessed the space over unpaid rent. Restaurant Online (2020-07-17) and Difford's Guide ('permanently closed') agree.

name: Momofuku Ssam Bar
evidence: Time Out New York (2023-09-11) reports Ssam Bar, by then at Pier 17 (moved from East Village in 2021), shutting on 2023-09-30. OpenTable and NYC Tourism list it as permanently closed / out of business; no relocation noted.
notes: Original East Village Ssam Bar (207 Second Ave) moved to Pier 17, 89 South St, in 2021; Pier 17 site closed 2023.

name: The Varnish
evidence: AOL/LA Times piece dated 2024-07-02 reports The Varnish, the bar inside Cole's at 118 E 6th St, would close its doors Wednesday 2024-07-03 after 15 years, co-owner Eric Alperin saying it is time to 'put her to sleep'. The Infatuation page also shows it permanently closed.
notes: Cole's itself was scheduled to close January 2026 (Airmail, 2026-01-10). No post-closure confirmation or reopening seen.

name: Whistling Shop
evidence: The Spirits Business reports owners Aske and Stephenson announced on 2018-11-05 that Worship Street Whistling Shop (63 Worship St, Shoreditch) closed; the site was to reopen as a London Cocktail Club. Time Out London carries a Nov 2018 note that it is now closed.
notes: Successor on the site is London Cocktail Club, a different business. No later relocation of the Whistling Shop found.

name: Der Raum
evidence: Australian Bartender's 2013-06-20 'Bar Economico opens this Saturday' article says Der Raum's Melbourne site was being reused for a new bar and that Der Raum was moving to Munich. No Melbourne Der Raum listing found since.
notes: Only a Melbourne-based relocation-to-Munich statement seen; Munich status not checked. Site is now Bar Economico (successor).

name: Hibiscus
evidence: Hot Dinners (2016-08-31) reported Hibiscus at 29 Maddox St, Mayfair closing at the start of October 2016, with chef Claude Bosi promising a new restaurant the following year. OpenTable says 'permanently closed' and Wikipedia says it closed in 2016.
notes: Bosi's later restaurant was a different venture (Bibendum building per The Caterer headline); no London Hibiscus relaunch seen.

name: Matterhorn
evidence: Restaurant & Cafe NZ and The Post (2017-07-26) report the Cuba Street Matterhorn closing in October 2017 after 54 years because earthquake damage to the neighbouring building required strengthening. Concrete Playground lists it as CLOSED.
notes: Concrete Playground page title shows 'Bar Te Aro' in the amp URL; not checked whether a new business uses the site.

name: BlueFrog Media Pvt. Ltd.
evidence: Local Press (2016-08-12) reports blueFROG's Lower Parel venue (Mathuradas Mills Compound) closing 2016-08-28; Toit took the space. Mixmag Asia (2025-11-03) says a relaunch is planned in Ballard Estate for early 2026; Time Out Mumbai lists Blue Frog among announced experiences at The Ballard Pier, which was set to open 2026-10-23 in phases, not confirmed open.
notes: Name is a company name; the real venue is blueFROG (Lower Parel). A new blueFROG at Ballard Pier/Ballard Estate, Fort is planned but no confirmation it has opened; treat as a possible MOVED to verify later.

name: Buddha-Bar London
evidence: The Caterer (2010-05-20) reports Buddha Bar on Victoria Embankment went into administration and ceased trading immediately, 80 staff made redundant. The later Knightsbridge relaunch (145 Knightsbridge, opened 2012) is marked 'permanently closed' on OpenTable and '(CLOSED)' on Time Out (page dated 2015-11-03).
notes: Two London sites: Embankment (closed 2010, 2010 W50B listing) and Knightsbridge (2012 reopening, closure shown only on undated labels). Former Embankment site was sold (The Caterer headline).

name: Tetsuya's Restaurant
evidence: Time Out Sydney (2024-05-14) reports Tetsuya's on Kent Street closing permanently with final service on 2024-07-31; chef Tetsuya Wakuda said plans to relocate had not worked out. Broadsheet, Gourmet Traveller, Hospitality Magazine and Concrete Playground carried the same announcement.
notes: No relocation seen.

name: Bayswater Brasserie
evidence: Australian Bartender (2010-09-15) says Bayswater Brasserie is officially gone and the Kings Cross / Potts Point site was leased by the Kingsley's owner to become Smith's Butcher and Wine Merchant. A 2022 Good Food headline says the former landmark became a Greek restaurant (Eros).
notes: Successor businesses on the site are different venues. Good Food page failed to open; its headline came from search results.

name: Double Happy
evidence: The Big City (page stamped 2026-04-14) describes Double Happy at 182 Cashel Street as a bar and club opened December 2006 that operated until the 2011 earthquakes, and lists it as closed. No reopening found.
notes: Single source; the page date is a page stamp rather than a dated closure article. Eventfinda page was blocked by robots.

name: Match Bar
evidence: CAMRA lists the Match bar at 37-38 Margaret Street as permanently closed (closed 21 Dec 2014; reopened June 2019 as a MEATliquor site, itself not listed as open). DesignMyNight (last modified 2021-03) says 'Match Bar has now closed'; a Match EC1 listing is also marked closed.
notes: Match Bar had several London sites (Margaret St, Clerkenwell EC1); none found open. Successor on the Margaret St site was MEATliquor (2019).

name: The Square
evidence: BigHospitality (2020-02-03) reported The Square, 6-10 Bruton Street, closed mid-lunch service when administrators seized assets of owner Marlon Abela. Hot Dinners (2021-11-22) says it closed in 2019/2020 and the site became SeaSons, a seafood restaurant.
notes: Successor business SeaSons at 6-10 Bruton St W1J 6PU is a different restaurant. Original Phil Howard era ended 2016 on sale to Abela.

name: Bagatelle
evidence: News in English (2014-09-03) reports Bagatelle, Norway's first two-Michelin-star restaurant, closed after years of losses; owner Christen Sveaas said 'we just couldn't make it work'. Wikipedia also gives closure as September 2014.
notes: Reopened briefly in 2012 after chef Hellstrom left, then closed for good 2014.

name: Thornton's Restaurant
evidence: Irish Times and The Taste (2016-09-01) report Kevin Thornton closing Thornton's at the Fitzwilliam Hotel, St Stephen's Green, last service 29 Oct 2016, after lease expiry and loss of Michelin star. No reopening found.
notes: Thornton moved to masterclasses and catering, not a new restaurant.

name: Changa
evidence: Frommer's (undated) says the original Changa (Sıraselviler Cad. 47, opened 1999) closed in 2014 and its operations moved to sister MüzedeChanga at the Sakıp Sabancı Museum. Sabah (2016-12-25) writes of Changa in the past tense and says the two owners retired.
notes: MüzedeChanga (Sakıp Sabancı Museum, Emirgan) appears open per Frommer's but is a separate sister venue, not verified for current status. Official Changa site blocked to fetch. Could be treated as MOVED if the team counts MüzedeChanga as the continuation.

name: Tangerine
evidence: Philadelphia Inquirer: Tangerine, 232 Market St, served its last meal on 8 Aug 2009. Inquirer (2013-03-14) says the 9,500 sq ft space was back on the market almost four years after closing.
notes: An Inquirer archive page dated 2026-04-28 is only a reprint of a 2000 review, not evidence of being open. Starr had said he might retool it in 2010; no reopening found.
